WITH type_averages AS (
  SELECT production_type_code,
         AVG(unit_price) AS type_avg_price
  FROM Products
  WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY production_type_code
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(type_avg_price) AS baseline_price
  FROM type_averages
),
above_baseline AS (
  SELECT ta.production_type_code,
         ta.type_avg_price
  FROM type_averages ta
  CROSS JOIN baseline
  WHERE ta.type_avg_price > baseline.baseline_price
),
mean_of_kept AS (
  SELECT AVG(type_avg_price) AS mean_price
  FROM above_baseline
),
final_types AS (
  SELECT ab.production_type_code,
         ab.type_avg_price
  FROM above_baseline ab
  CROSS JOIN mean_of_kept
  WHERE ab.type_avg_price > mean_of_kept.mean_price
)
SELECT AVG(ft.type_avg_price) AS avg_type_price,
       AVG(ft.type_avg_price - b.baseline_price) AS avg_above_baseline,
       AVG(ft.type_avg_price - m.mean_price) AS avg_above_kept_mean
FROM final_types ft
CROSS JOIN baseline b
CROSS JOIN mean_of_kept m
WHERE b.baseline_price IS NOT NULL

assumptions.assumption: If baseline is NULL (no products with valid prices) or no types pass both filtering conditions, the query returns zero rows rather than one row with NULL values. The request's 'return one row' implicitly assumes the data contains at least one type satisfying both filters.
